inheritance.title: Inheritance and Modular Design
whereToLook: Check that Astronaut is declared with 'extends Employee' so it inherits name, ID, and salary instead of redefining them.
Check that both Astronaut constructors call super(...) so the Employee part of the object gets built.
Astronaut should only add mission name and mission role — everything else comes from Employee.

scanner-input.title: Reading Input with Scanner
whereToLook: Check that you created one Scanner and used it to read every value the user enters.
Check that each prompt is printed before you read the matching value.
If a value after the salary looks empty or wrong, check whether a leftover newline is being read into the next field.

encapsulation.title: Fields, Constructors, Getters, and Setters
whereToLook: Check that Employee and Astronaut store their data in fields, not just local variables in EmployeeManager.
Check that your no-arg constructors set fields to the empty-string/0.0 defaults described in the README.
Check that your overload constructors assign every parameter to the matching field.
Check that EmployeeManager builds its output using the getter methods on the Astronaut object, not the original input variables.

output-formatting.title: Displaying the Astronaut's Data
whereToLook: Check that each line of output uses the exact label shown in the README, followed by a colon, a space, and the value.
Check that the five lines are printed in the same order shown in the README.
Check that you are printing the astronaut built from user input, not the no-arg one.

sourceChecks.name: Uses Scanner for input
sourceChecks.message: This challenge requires you to use a Scanner to read the astronaut's information from the user.

sourceChecks.name: Creates an Astronaut with the no-arg constructor
sourceChecks.message: The README asks you to create a second Astronaut object using the no-arg constructor to confirm it works. Look for a line like 'new Astronaut()' in EmployeeManager.

sourceChecks.name: Creates an Astronaut with the overload constructor
sourceChecks.message: Check that you are creating an Astronaut object with the overload constructor, passing it the name, ID, salary, mission name, and mission role.

tests.name: Displays astronaut data entered by the user (Buzz Aldrin)
tests.input:
Buzz Aldrin
AST001
100000.0
Apollo 11
Lunar Module Pilot
tests.expectedOutput:
Name: Buzz Aldrin
ID: AST001
Salary: 100000.0
Mission Name: Apollo 11
Mission Role: Lunar Module Pilot
tests.message: Check that your program reads all five prompts with Scanner, builds an Astronaut with the overload constructor, and displays its data using the getter methods in the exact order and label format shown in the README.

possibleErrors.message: No output was produced. Make sure Employee.java and Astronaut.java both compile (they need a class declaration, fields, and constructors) and that EmployeeManager actually prints the astronaut's data.
